summary: Eight concrete, comment-endorsed tools and resources surfaced from the verified HN front-page comment crawl.
telegram_footer: 8 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: Camoufox
items.source_story_title: My server is a phone now
items.summary: A browser automation tool a commenter runs at high density on a cheap VPS.
items.why_included: It received an unambiguous practical recommendation backed by direct first-hand use.
items.evidence: A commenter says they run ten Camoufox instances on an $8 VPS and highly recommends it.

evidence_sources.author: hackernud3s
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've never heard of Surf but I can run 10x camoufox instances on a $8 VPS no problem. I highly recommend it.

items.name: OrbStack
items.source_story_title: My server is a phone now
items.summary: A macOS container runtime that uses native containerization APIs instead of Docker Desktop.
items.why_included: A first-hand Mac user named it their preferred Docker runtime and cited performance.
items.evidence: A commenter calls OrbStack their go-to for Docker on Mac and says its native APIs improve performance.

evidence_sources.author: chrisldgk
evidence_sources.excerpt: OrbStack is my go-to when it comes to running docker on Mac. It also uses macOS native containerization APIs so containers will be a bit more performant than they would (at least use to) be on Docker Desktop.

items.name: Red Blob Games
items.summary: An interactive programming and game-development reference site, especially strong on pathfinding.
items.why_included: The site received a direct high-confidence recommendation from a reader of its pathfinding work.
items.evidence: A commenter says Red Blob Games has several S-tier posts and highly recommends exploring it.

evidence_sources.author: Groxx
evidence_sources.excerpt: Red Blob Games has quite a few S-tier posts, highly recommend exploring further if this is at all interesting to you

items.name: NBA*
items.summary: A JavaScript graph-pathfinding library featuring the NBA* bidirectional A* algorithm.
items.why_included: It was singled out as a pathfinding implementation that has consistently impressed its user.
items.evidence: A commenter says they have always been impressed by NBA* and links its repository and demo.

evidence_sources.author: leeoniya
evidence_sources.excerpt: i've always been impressed by NBA*:

items.name: Wego
items.source_story_title: Windows 11's built-in Weather app wastes more than 1 GB of RAM
items.summary: A terminal weather app that one long-term user found dependable with minimal maintenance.
items.why_included: It has a rare decade-scale first-hand endorsement for a deliberately small weather tool.
items.evidence: A commenter reports using Wego for roughly a decade and needing only one configuration change.

evidence_sources.author: Hackbraten
evidence_sources.excerpt: I’ve used Wego [0] for roughly a decade. It’s been good enough for me.

items.name: reManager
items.source_story_title: Reviving a four year old reMarkable 2
items.summary: A reMarkable tablet management tool for installing apps and transferring large files.
items.why_included: It solved a detailed real-world reMarkable setup problem without firmware changes.
items.evidence: A reMarkable owner says reManager worked out of the box, installed KoReader, and transferred large files.

evidence_sources.author: haskman
evidence_sources.excerpt: It just worked out of the box, did not require a firmware update, and I was able to install KoReader and other goodies

items.name: QArt Codes
items.summary: Russ Cox's technical write-up on embedding images in valid QR codes through encoding.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly treats the post as the canonical resource for the technique.
items.evidence: A commenter says they always think of Russ Cox's QArt posts as canonical.

evidence_sources.author: zellyn
evidence_sources.excerpt: I always think of Russ Cox’s blog posts as canonical here:

items.name: Termic
items.summary: A desktop manager for coding-agent worktrees, terminals, diffs, and inline feedback.
items.why_included: It received a specific recommendation for its focused design and active maintenance.
items.evidence: A commenter highly recommends Termic, saying it works well and its developer is responsive.

evidence_sources.author: 0xbadcafebee
evidence_sources.excerpt: As a simpler desktop-only multi-platform option, I can highly recommend Termic
